lessons.title: SELECT: ask for the columns you want
lessons.intro: Hiii! Today we learn how to ask a table for exactly what you want.
lessons.easy_words: A table is a spreadsheet that answers questions. If you ask for everything, it's like asking a waiter for 'the whole menu'. Sweet, but chaotic. SELECT lets you order only the dishes you want. (And if you ever DO want everything, a star * means 'all columns'.)
lessons.syntax_note: SELECT = what you want, FROM = where it lives, ; = 'that's my order, thanks'.
lessons.example_result: Boom, you get just names and marks. No drama. 🍬
lessons.task: Show me each student's name and city. I believe in you!
lessons.hint: Put the two column names after SELECT, with a comma between them, then say FROM students.
lessons.retry: Ooh, so close! That one brought extra columns to the party. We only invited name and city. Try once more?
lessons.cheer: Yesss! Exactly the two columns we invited. Table whisperer, that's you.

lessons.title: WHERE: keep only the rows you want
lessons.intro: Nice work! Now let's make the table pick favourites.
lessons.easy_words: WHERE is a bouncer at the door. Every row has to pass your rule to get in. You can compare with = (equal), > (bigger), and < (smaller). Words like city names go inside single quotes, because the table is picky about text.
lessons.syntax_note: The condition is the bouncer's rule, like course = 'BCA' or marks > 70.
lessons.example_result: Only the BCA students get in. Everyone else waits outside. 🚪
lessons.task: Show all columns for students from Pune.
lessons.hint: Use SELECT * to get all columns, then WHERE city = 'Pune'. Don't forget the single quotes around Pune.
lessons.retry: Almost! The bouncer is a bit confused. Check the rule after WHERE, and remember text goes in single quotes. Try again?
lessons.cheer: Perfect! The bouncer let only the Pune crowd in. Strict but fair.

lessons.title: ORDER BY and LIMIT: sort and cut the list
lessons.intro: You're on a roll! Time to line everyone up.
lessons.easy_words: ORDER BY lines the rows up, like a queue. DESC means biggest first, and ASC (the default) means smallest first. LIMIT says 'only the first few, please', like taking only the top slices of a pizza.
lessons.syntax:
SELECT columns
FROM table_name
ORDER BY column DESC
LIMIT number;
lessons.syntax_note: Swap DESC for ASC to flip the queue. LIMIT always goes last.
lessons.example: SELECT name, joined_year FROM students ORDER BY joined_year LIMIT 2;
lessons.example_result: The two earliest joiners, first in line. Respect the veterans. 🍕
lessons.task: Show all columns for the 3 students with the highest marks.
lessons.expected_query: SELECT * FROM students ORDER BY marks DESC LIMIT 3;
lessons.hint: Sort by marks with DESC so the biggest comes first, then LIMIT 3.
lessons.retry: So close! The queue is in the wrong order, or too long. Highest marks first, and only 3 people. Try again?
lessons.cheer: Top 3 on the podium. Gold, silver, bronze, and you get a gold star too.

lessons.title: DISTINCT: no repeats, please
lessons.intro: Last lesson of the stage. You're almost a SQL person!
lessons.easy_words: Sometimes a column repeats the same value again and again, like 'Pune' showing up three times. DISTINCT says 'I've heard that one already, show it once'.
lessons.example_result: Each city appears exactly once. Clean and tidy. ✨
lessons.hint: Put DISTINCT right after SELECT, then the column name course.
lessons.retry: Hmm, some courses are showing up twice. Remember the magic word DISTINCT right after SELECT. Try again?
lessons.cheer: Squeaky clean list! No repeats anywhere.

project.title: Stage 1 project: 5 questions about the students
project.intro: Project time! Five questions, and you've got every tool you need. Take your time.

tasks.question: Show the name and marks of students with more than 80 marks.
tasks.expected_query: SELECT name, marks FROM students WHERE marks > 80;
tasks.hint: Use WHERE with the > sign on marks.

tasks.question: Show all columns for students who joined in 2022.
tasks.hint: Numbers don't need quotes. Use WHERE joined_year = 2022.

tasks.question: Show the name and marks of the 2 lowest scorers.
tasks.expected_query: SELECT name, marks FROM students ORDER BY marks ASC LIMIT 2;
tasks.hint: Sort ascending so the smallest marks come first, then LIMIT 2.

tasks.question: Show all columns for BCA students, sorted by name from A to Z.
tasks.expected_query: SELECT * FROM students WHERE course = 'BCA' ORDER BY name;
tasks.hint: Combine WHERE for the course and ORDER BY name. WHERE comes before ORDER BY.

project.cheer: Stage 1 complete! You can now read data from a table like a pro. Ready for Stage 2?
